title: Teaching CS50 with AI - David J. Malan
summary: David Malan describes CS50's guardrailed AI 'duck' tutor: design, usage, accuracy and how it shifted student help-seeking.

assertions.quote: just directly using something like ChatGPT would have definitely detracted from learning

verdicts.note: Anthropic's 2026 study found high scorers used AI for conceptual questions and explanations while low scorers delegated; small sample and a single learning task.

assertions.quote: I love how AI bots will answer the questions without ego and without judgment

verdicts.note: Some RCTs (e.g. a Harvard physics AI-tutor study) show learning gains when tutors are scaffolded, but hallucinations and answer-giving can undermine learning.

assertions.quote: It will save humans time, and it will amplify the impact of individual humans, much more so, for instance, than replacing them outright.

verdicts.note: Through 2026 evidence points to role change and slower junior hiring, not elimination of the profession; long-run is uncertain.

assertions.quote: I do think this problem will go further and further away over time as the technology gets better.

verdicts.note: Hallucination rates have fallen markedly in newer models, but they remain non-zero, especially on obscure facts, and are structurally hard to eliminate.

assertions.quote: you use English or your own human language to tell the AI how to behave

verdicts.note: A framing of how software is built rather than a testable factual claim; widely adopted as a lens.

assertions.quote: the duck answered 88% of curricular questions, content questions, correctly

verdicts.note: Several course deployments report high accuracy on intro-level content questions, though accuracy drops on course-specific policy and advanced material.

assertions.quote: fewer students were taking advantage, funny enough, of those same human resources

verdicts.note: Course reports show drops in forum posts and office-hour attendance after AI tutors launch, but the evidence is observational and confounded.
